summary: troubleshooting@1.0.0 exfiltrates host identity to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and on require
details: The package is a stub whose `index.js` exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for every property access, so any importer appears to succeed while a beacon fires silently. The `postinstall` hook runs `beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` also invokes the same beacon on require. The beacon POSTs JSON containing `os.hostname()`, the install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and the node/npm version to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` over plain HTTP. The destination is not a publisher-owned host; the package description is only `Compatibility shim`, and the generic name combined with the stub-with-Proxy shape is consistent with a dependency-confusion payload. Installing or requiring the package leaks installer host and install-path identifiers to an attacker-controlled bare-IP endpoint without disclosure or opt-in.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
